                    if rx.search(line):
                        add(rule, sev, path, i, line.strip()[:100], fix)
                if "console.log(" in line:
                    console_logs += 1
                if re.search(r"\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b", line):
                    todos += 1
        if base == "package.json":
            try:
                pkg = json.loads("\n".join(lines))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pkg = {}
            d = os.path.dirname(path)
            if not any(
                os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, lf))
                for lf in ("package-lock.json", "yarn.lock", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "bun.lockb", "bun.lock")
            ):
                add(
                    "no_lockfile",
                    "medium",
                    path,
                    0,
                    "no lockfile next to package.json",
                    "Commit your lockfile so installs are reproducible.",
                )
            for section in ("dependencies", "devDependencies"):
                for dep, ver in (pkg.get(section) or {}).items():
                    if ver in {"*", "latest", ""}:
                        add("unpinned_dep", "medium", path, 0, f"{dep}@{ver}", "Pin to a specific version range.")

    if env_vars and not any(
        os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) for f in (".env.example", ".env.sample", ".env.template")
    ):
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding(
                "missing_env_example",
                "low",
                ".env.example",
                0,
                f"{len(env_vars)} env vars referenced, no .env.example",
                "Run with --fix to generate one.",
            )
        )
    if not has_tests:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding(
                "no_tests",
                "medium",
                "-",
                0,
                "no test files found",
                "Add smoke tests for sign-up, payment and core flows.",
            )
        )
    if not any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) for f in ("README.md", "readme.md", "README")):
        rep.findings.append(Finding("no_readme", "low", "-", 0, "no README", "Document how to run and deploy the app."))
    if console_logs > 10:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding("console_logs", "low", "-", 0, f"{console_logs} console.log calls", "Remove or gate debug logging.")
        )
    if todos > 10:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding("todos", "low", "-", 0, f"{todos} TODO/FIXME markers", "Turn them into tracked issues.")
        )

    rep.env_vars = sorted(env_vars)
    sev_rank = {"critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 3}
    rep.findings.sort(key=lambda f: (sev_rank[f.severity], f.file, f.line))
    penalty = sum(SEVERITY_POINTS[f.severity] for f in rep.findings)
    rep.score = max(0, 100 - penalty)
    rep.grade = (
        "A"
        if rep.score >= 90
        else "B"
        if rep.score >= 75
        else "C"
        if rep.score >= 60
        else "D"
        if rep.score >= 40
        else "F"
    )
    rules = {f.rule for f in rep.findings}
    rep.quote_minutes = sum(SERVICE_MENU[r][1] for r in rules)
    rep.quote_usd = sum(SERVICE_MENU[r][2] for r in rules)
    return rep


def apply_safe_fixes(root: str, rep: Report) -> list[str]:
    """Only non-destructive fixes: git-ignore env files, write .env.example with names (never values)."""
    done = []
    rules = {f.rule for f in rep.findings}
    if "env_not_ignored" in rules:
        gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
        existing = ""
        if os.path.exists(gi):
            with open(gi, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
                existing = fh.read()
        add = [p for p in (".env", ".env.*", "!.env.example") if p not in existing.split()]
        with open(gi, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(("\n" if existing and not existing.endswith("\n") else "") + "\n".join(add) + "\n")
        done.append(f"added {', '.join(add)} to .gitignore (rotate any keys that were committed!)")
    if "missing_env_example" in rules and rep.env_vars:
        try:  # "x": never overwrite a .env.example the user already has
            with open(os.path.join(root, ".env.example"), "x", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write("# Generated by vibe-lube - fill in real values in .env (never commit it)\n")
                fh.write("".join(f"{v}=\n" for v in rep.env_vars))
            done.append(f"wrote .env.example with {len(rep.env_vars)} variables")
        except FileExistsError:
            done.append("left existing .env.example untouched")
    return done

      "name": "vibe_lube/web.py",
      "content": """"Hosted API and web app for this product, generated from its CLI (shared runtime, identical in every product).

Every CLI command becomes POST /api/<command> (JSON in, JSON out) and a form at GET /. Each request runs the
real CLI in an isolated subprocess with a timeout, so the web app and the CLI can never disagree.

Security model:
- File and folder arguments come only from uploads written into a private per-request directory; a client can
  never name a path on the server. Folder uploads are zip archives extracted with path-traversal checks.
- Values are passed as separate argv items, options as --flag=value and positionals after "--", so user text
  can never become an option or a shell command.
- State/store options are pinned by the server to its data directory (--data-dir), never client-controlled.
- 5 MB request cap, 30 s run timeout, CSP / nosniff / frame-deny headers, binds 127.0.0.1 unless --host is set.

Run:  <product>-web --port 8000 [--host 0.0.0.0] [--data-dir ./data]
"""

    "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",

class BadRequest(ValueError):
    pass


def _write_upload(field: dict, value, workdir: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    """Materialise an uploaded file or folder inside workdir and return its path."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: expected an upload object")
    if field["kind"] == "dir":
        target = workdir / f"in-{field['dest']}"
        target.mkdir()
        if "files" in value:  # [{"name": "a.txt", "content": "..."}]
            for f in value["files"]:
                _safe_member(target, str(f.get("name", ""))).write_text(str(f.get("content", "")), encoding="utf-8")
        elif "base64" in value:  # a zip archive
            try:
                with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(value["base64"], validate=True))) as z:
                    for info in z.infolist():
                        if not info.is_dir():
                            _safe_member(target, info.filename).write_bytes(z.read(info))
            except (zipfile.BadZipFile, ValueError) as e:
                raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: not a valid zip archive ({e})") from None
        else:
            raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: folder uploads need 'files' or a base64 zip")
        return str(target)
    name = pathlib.PurePath(str(value.get("name") or field["dest"])).name or field["dest"]
    path = workdir / f"in-{field['dest']}-{name}"
    if "base64" in value:
        try:
            path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(value["base64"], validate=True))
        except ValueError:
            raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: invalid base64") from None
    else:
        path.write_text(str(value.get("content", "")), encoding="utf-8")
    return str(path)


def _safe_member(root: pathlib.Path, name: str) -> pathlib.Path:
    dest = (root / name).resolve()
    if root.resolve() not in dest.parents:
        raise BadRequest(f"unsafe path in upload: {name!r}")
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return dest


def build_argv(op: dict, payload: dict, workdir: pathlib.Path, data_dir: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[list, dict]:
    """Translate a JSON payload into CLI argv. Returns (argv, outputs) where outputs maps dest -> output path."""
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise BadRequest("request body must be a JSON object")
    unknown = set(payload) - {f["dest"] for f in op["fields"]}
    if unknown:
        raise BadRequest(f"unknown fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
    head, opts, pos, outputs = [], [], [], {}
    for flag, filename in SPEC.get("state", {}).items():  # server-pinned stores go before the subcommand
        head.append(f"{flag}={data_dir / filename}")
    for f in op["fields"]:
        kind, value = f["kind"], payload.get(f["dest"])
        if kind == "output":
            value = str(workdir / f"out-{f['dest']}")
            outputs[f["dest"]] = value
        elif kind == "state":  # a per-command store: always the server's own file, never client-chosen
            value = str(data_dir / f["file"])
        elif value is None or value == "" or value == []:
            if f.get("required"):
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} is required")
            continue
        elif kind in ("file", "dir"):
            value = _write_upload(f, value, workdir)
        elif kind == "bool":
            if value is True:
                (head if f.get("scope") == "global" else opts).append(f["flag"])
            continue
        elif kind in ("int", "number"):
            try:
                value = str(int(value) if kind == "int" else float(value))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} must be a number") from None
        elif kind == "list":
            values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
            if f.get("choices") and any(str(v) not in f["choices"] for v in values):
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} must be among {f['choices']}")
            if f["flag"] is None:
                pos.extend(str(v) for v in values)
            elif f.get("append"):
                opts.extend(f"{f['flag']}={v}" for v in values)
            elif values:  # nargs list option: items follow the flag, so none may look like an option
                if any(str(v).startswith("-") for v in values):
                    raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} items cannot start with '-'")
                opts.extend([f["flag"], *[str(v) for v in values]])
            continue
        else:
            value = str(value)
            if f.get("choices") and value not in f["choices"]:
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} must be one of {f['choices']}")
        if f["flag"] is None:
            pos.append(value)
        else:
            (head if f.get("scope") == "global" else opts).append(f"{f['flag']}={value}")
    # positionals after "--" so user text that starts with "-" can never be read as an option
    argv = [*head, *op["prefix"], *opts]
    if pos:
        argv += ["--", *pos]
    return argv, outputs


def run_op(op: dict, payload: dict, data_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="web-") as tmp:
        work = pathlib.Path(tmp)
        argv, outputs = build_argv(op, payload, work, data_dir)
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "AGENT_ECONOMY_DEBUG"}
        env.update(PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8", HOME=str(data_dir), USERPROFILE=str(data_dir))
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-m", PKG, *argv],
                cwd=work,
                env=env,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                encoding="utf-8",
                errors="replace",
                timeout=TIMEOUT,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {"ok": False, "exit_code": None, "error": f"timed out after {TIMEOUT}s"}
        # exit 1 is a domain answer ("nothing found", "failing grade") only when the command said something;
        # a silent exit 1 is a failure, and stderr is always passed through so the user sees why
        # never echo the server's private temp paths back to the client
        r.stdout = r.stdout.replace(str(work), "upload").replace(str(work.resolve()), "upload")
        r.stderr = r.stderr.replace(str(work), "upload").replace(str(work.resolve()), "upload")
        said = bool(r.stdout.strip())
        result = {
            "ok": r.returncode == 0 or (r.returncode == 1 and said),
            "exit_code": r.returncode,
            "stdout": r.stdout[-200_000:],
        }
        if r.stderr.strip():
            result["stderr"] = r.stderr.strip()[-2000:]
        if not result["ok"]:
            result["error"] = result.get("stderr") or "command failed without output"
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            result["json"] = json.loads(r.stdout)
        for dest, path in outputs.items():
            p = pathlib.Path(path)
            if p.is_file():
                result.setdefault("files", {})[dest] = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[-500_000:]
        return result


class Gate:
    """API keys, a per-caller rate limit and usage metering (the record billing is built on).

    Keys come from API_KEYS (comma-separated) and/or <data-dir>/api-keys.json, which stores only SHA-256
    hashes. With no keys configured the API is open, which `main` allows only on a loopback address.
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: pathlib.Path, env_keys: str = "", rate_per_min: int = 60):
        self.keys_file, self.usage_file = data_dir / "api-keys.json", data_dir / "usage.jsonl"
        self.env = {_digest(k.strip()): f"env-{i}" for i, k in enumerate(env_keys.split(","), 1) if k.strip()}
        self.rate = rate_per_min
        self.hits: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def stored(self) -> dict:
        try:
            data = json.loads(self.keys_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return {}
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}

    def active(self) -> dict:
        """hash -> key id for every key that may call the API."""
        keys = dict(self.env)
        keys.update({rec["hash"]: kid for kid, rec in self.stored().items() if not rec.get("revoked")})
        return keys

    def required(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.active())

    def identify(self, header: str | None) -> str | None:
        if not header or not header.startswith("Bearer "):
            return None
        digest = _digest(header[7:].strip())
        found = None
        for h, kid in self.active().items():  # compare every key in constant time; never short-circuit
            if hmac.compare_digest(h, digest):
                found = kid
        return found

    def retry_after(self, caller: str) -> int | None:
        """Sliding one-minute window; returns seconds to wait when the caller is over the limit."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        with self.lock:
            window = [t for t in self.hits.get(caller, []) if now - t < 60]
            if len(window) >= self.rate:
                self.hits[caller] = window
                return max(1, int(60 - (now - window[0])) + 1)
            window.append(now)
            self.hits[caller] = window
        return None

    def record(self, caller: str, op: str, status: int, ms: int):
        line = json.dumps(
            {
                "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
                "key": caller,
                "op": op,
                "status": status,
                "ms": ms,
            }
        )
        with self.lock, open(self.usage_file, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(line + "\n")

    def create(self, label: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key = "sk_" + secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        digest = _digest(key)
        kid = digest[:10]
        keys = self.stored()
        keys[kid] = {"hash": digest, "label": label, "created": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), "revoked": False}
        self._save(keys)
        return kid, key

    def revoke(self, kid: str) -> bool:
        keys = self.stored()
        if kid not in keys:
            return False
        keys[kid]["revoked"] = True
        self._save(keys)
        return True

    def _save(self, keys: dict):
        tmp = self.keys_file.with_suffix(".tmp")
        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(keys, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        os.replace(tmp, self.keys_file)

    def usage(self) -> dict:
        summary: dict[str, dict] = {}
        try:
            lines = self.usage_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return summary
        for ln in lines:
            with contextlib.suppress(ValueError, KeyError):
                rec = json.loads(ln)
                s = summary.setdefault(rec["key"], {"calls": 0, "ok": 0, "by_op": {}})
                s["calls"] += 1
                s["ok"] += rec["status"] == 200
                s["by_op"][rec["op"]] = s["by_op"].get(rec["op"], 0) + 1
        return summary


def _digest(key: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = f"{PKG}-web"
    data_dir: pathlib.Path
    gate: Gate

    def _send(self, status: int, body: bytes, ctype: str, extra: dict | None = None):
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        for k, v in {**HEADERS, **(extra or {})}.items():
            self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _json(self, status: int, obj, extra: dict | None = None):
        body = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
        self._send(status, body, "application/json; charset=utf-8", extra)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # one line per request on stderr, no bodies
        sys.stderr.write(f"{self.address_string()} {fmt % args}\n")

    def do_GET(self):
        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
        if path == "/healthz":
            self._json(200, {"status": "ok", "product": SPEC["name"]})
        elif path == "/api/spec":
            self._json(200, SPEC)
        elif path == "/app.js":
            self._send(200, APP_JS.encode("utf-8"), "text/javascript; charset=utf-8")
        elif path in ("/", "/index.html"):
            self._send(200, page().encode("utf-8"), "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        else:
            self._json(404, {"error": "not found"})

    def do_POST(self):
        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
        try:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
        except ValueError:
            return self._json(400, {"error": "bad Content-Length"})
        if length > MAX_BODY:
            return self._json(HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, {"error": f"request over {MAX_BODY} bytes"})
        # always read the body before answering: closing with unread data makes some stacks reset the connection
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        op = OPS.get(path.removeprefix("/api/")) if path.startswith("/api/") else None
        if not op:
            return self._json(404, {"error": "unknown command", "commands": sorted(OPS)})
        caller = self.gate.identify(self.headers.get("Authorization"))
        if caller is None and self.gate.required():
            self.gate.record("unauthenticated", op["id"], 401, 0)
            return self._json(401, {"error": "missing or invalid API key"}, {"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
        caller = caller or f"ip:{self.client_address[0]}"
        wait = self.gate.retry_after(caller)
        if wait:
            return self._json(
                429, {"error": f"rate limit: {self.gate.rate} requests per minute"}, {"Retry-After": str(wait)}
            )
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            payload = json.loads(body or b"{}")
            result = run_op(op, payload, self.data_dir)
            status = 200
        except (ValueError, BadRequest) as e:
            result, status = {"error": str(e)}, 400
        self.gate.record(caller, op["id"], status, int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))
        self._json(status, result)


def page() -> str:
    import html

    e = html.escape
    forms = []
    for op in SPEC["ops"]:
        rows = []
        for f in op["fields"]:
            if f["kind"] in ("output", "state"):
                continue
            label = e(f["dest"].replace("_", " ")) + (" *" if f.get("required") else "")
            hint = f"<small>{e(f.get('help') or '')}</small>" if f.get("help") else ""
            name = e(f["dest"])
            if f["kind"] == "bool":
                ctl = f'<input type="checkbox" name="{name}">'
            elif f.get("choices") and f["kind"] != "list":
                opts = "".join(f"<option>{e(str(c))}</option>" for c in f["choices"])
                ctl = f'<select name="{name}"><option value=""></option>{opts}</select>'
            elif f["kind"] == "file":
                ctl = f'<textarea name="{name}" data-kind="file" rows="6" placeholder="paste file contents or choose a file"></textarea><input type="file" data-for="{name}">'
            elif f["kind"] == "dir":
                ctl = f'<input type="file" name="{name}" data-kind="dir" multiple><small>choose files, or one .zip</small>'
            else:
                typ = "number" if f["kind"] in ("int", "number") else "text"
                step = ' step="any"' if f["kind"] == "number" else ""
                ph = " (comma-separated)" if f["kind"] == "list" else ""
                default = "" if f.get("default") in (None, "") else e(str(f["default"]))
                ctl = f'<input type="{typ}"{step} name="{name}" data-kind="{e(f["kind"])}" placeholder="{default}{ph}">'
            rows.append(f"<label>{label}{ctl}{hint}</label>")
        forms.append(
            f'<section><h2>{e(op["title"])}</h2><form data-op="{e(op["id"])}">{"".join(rows)}'
            f'<button type="submit">Run</button></form><pre class="out" hidden></pre></section>'
        )
    return f"""<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8">

const readText = (f) => new Promise((ok, no) => { const r = new FileReader(); r.onload = () => ok(r.result); r.onerror = no; r.readAsText(f); });

try { document.getElementById('api-key').value = sessionStorage.getItem('apiKey') || ''; } catch (e) { /* storage blocked */ }

LOOPBACK = {"127.0.0.1", "localhost", "::1"}


def make_server(
    host: str, port: int, data_dir: pathlib.Path, env_keys: str = "", rate: int = 60
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gate = Gate(data_dir.resolve(), env_keys, rate)
    handler = type("BoundHandler", (Handler,), {"data_dir": data_dir.resolve(), "gate": gate})
    return ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), handler)


def keys_main(argv: list) -> int:
    """<cli>-web keys create|list|revoke and <cli>-web usage: manage API keys and read metering."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=f"{SPEC['cli']}-web")
    ap.add_argument("--data-dir", default=os.environ.get("DATA_DIR", "data"))
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    k = sub.add_parser("keys").add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True)
    k.add_parser("create").add_argument("--label", required=True, help="who the key is for, e.g. a customer")
    k.add_parser("list")
    k.add_parser("revoke").add_argument("key_id")
    sub.add_parser("usage", help="calls per key, for billing")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    data_dir = pathlib.Path(a.data_dir)
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gate = Gate(data_dir.resolve())
    if a.cmd == "usage":
        print(json.dumps(gate.usage(), indent=2))
    elif a.action == "create":
        kid, key = gate.create(a.label)
        print(f"key id {kid} for {a.label!r}\n{key}\nShown once; only its hash is stored.")
    elif a.action == "list":
        for kid, rec in gate.stored().items():
            print(f"{kid}  {rec['created']}  {'REVOKED ' if rec.get('revoked') else ''}{rec['label']}")
    elif not gate.revoke(a.key_id):
        print(f"no key {a.key_id!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    else:
        print(f"revoked {a.key_id}")
    return 0


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if argv[:1] in (["keys"], ["usage"]) or (len(argv) > 2 and argv[2] in ("keys", "usage")):
        return keys_main(argv)
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=f"{SPEC['cli']}-web", description=f"{SPEC['name']} hosted API and web app")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--host", default="127.0.0.1", help="use 0.0.0.0 to accept outside connections (e.g. in a container)"
    )
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000")))
    ap.add_argument("--data-dir", default=os.environ.get("DATA_DIR", "data"), help="where server-side state is kept")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--rate", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN", "60")), help="calls/min per caller"
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--allow-public",
        action="store_true",
        default=os.environ.get("ALLOW_PUBLIC") == "1",
        help="serve a non-loopback address without API keys (not recommended)",
    )
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    srv = make_server(a.host, a.port, pathlib.Path(a.data_dir), os.environ.get("API_KEYS", ""), a.rate)
    gate = srv.RequestHandlerClass.gate
    if a.host not in LOOPBACK and not gate.required() and not a.allow_public:
        srv.server_close()
        print(
            f"refusing to serve {a.host} with no API keys: run `{SPEC['cli']}-web keys create --label NAME` "
            "or set API_KEYS (or pass --allow-public)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    access = "API keys required" if gate.required() else "open (no API keys)"
    print(
        f"{SPEC['name']} on http://{a.host}:{srv.server_address[1]}  ({access}; data: {pathlib.Path(a.data_dir).resolve()})"
    )
    with contextlib.suppress(KeyboardInterrupt):
        srv.serve_forever()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

      "name": "ARCHITECTURE.md",
      "content": "# Architecture — vibe-lube

## 1. Scope
Fast inspection and safe tune-ups for AI-built ("vibe-coded") apps.
**MVP:** repository walker (skips vendored and build directories) with detectors for secrets, env
hygiene, client-side secret exposure, supply chain, risky code and maintainability. Severity-weighted
health score and grade, a service menu quote, and safe auto-fixes only (`.gitignore` env entries,
names-only `.env.example`).
**Product:** GitHub App on every PR, runtime checks against the deployed URL, agent-generated fix PRs with human review.

## 2. System context
```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Repo[Repository] --> Walker
  Walker --> Detectors[Detectors: secrets, env, client exposure, supply chain, risky code, maintainability]
  Detectors --> Findings[(Findings)]
  Findings --> Score[Score + grade]
  Findings --> Menu[Service menu quote]
  Findings --> Fixer[Safe auto-fixer]
  Findings -->|book a mechanic| Human[Expert review]
```

## 3. Detector design
Each detector is a pure function over a file's lines (plus repo-level checks), emitting
`Finding{rule, severity, file, line, detail, fix}`. Secrets are **masked in findings**
(`first6...last2`) so reports are safe to share. Severity points are critical 25, high 12,
medium 5, low 1.

## 4. Design decisions
- **Safe fixes only, automatically.** Anything that could break the app (rotating keys,
  refactoring SQL) is a menu item for a human. Generated `.env.example` contains **names only, never values**.
- **Client-side heuristics** (`src/`, `app/`, `pages/`, `components/` minus `/api/`) to flag
  `service_role` and public-prefixed secrets. These are the most common catastrophic leaks in
  Supabase and Next.js vibe apps.
- **Placeholder suppression** (`example`, `xxxx`) cuts false positives in docs and tests.
- **Exit code reflects grade** (A–C → 0, D–F → 1) so it can gate CI.

## 5. Production architecture
A GitHub App (webhooks → job queue → sandboxed scanner container → check-run annotations).
Runtime probes (`/.env`, `/.git/config`, open Supabase tables via the anon key, missing RLS).
A fix-PR generator (agent) behind mandatory human approval.

## 6. Risks
Regex secret detection has false positives and negatives, so entropy checks and provider-specific
validators come next. Never transmit discovered secrets: masking happens at detection time.

import base64
import http.client
import io
import json
import os
import pathlib
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import zipfile

from vibe_lube import web
from vibe_lube._webspec import SPEC

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
EXAMPLES = json.loads((ROOT / "tests" / "web_examples.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


class WebAppTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        os.environ["PYTHONPATH"] = (
            str(ROOT) + os.pathsep + os.environ.get("PYTHONPATH", "")
        )  # subprocess finds the package
        cls.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        web.Handler.log_message = lambda *args: None  # keep test output readable
        cls.srv = web.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0, pathlib.Path(cls.tmp.name) / "data")
        cls.url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{cls.srv.server_address[1]}"
        threading.Thread(target=cls.srv.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()

    @classmethod
    def tearDownClass(cls):
        cls.srv.shutdown()
        cls.srv.server_close()
        cls.tmp.cleanup()

    def call(self, path, body=None, raw=None):
        data = raw if raw is not None else (None if body is None else json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8"))
        req = urllib.request.Request(self.url + path, data=data, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=90) as r:
                return r.status, r.headers, r.read()
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            with e:
                return e.code, e.headers, e.read()

    def test_health_spec_and_app_page(self):
        status, _, body = self.call("/healthz")
        self.assertEqual((status, json.loads(body)["status"]), (200, "ok"))
        status, headers, body = self.call("/")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("default-src 'none'", headers["Content-Security-Policy"])
        page = body.decode("utf-8")
        for op in SPEC["ops"]:
            self.assertIn(f'data-op="{op["id"]}"', page)
        self.assertEqual(self.call("/app.js")[0], 200)
        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.call("/api/spec")[2])["name"], SPEC["name"])

    def test_every_documented_command_works_over_the_api(self):
        self.assertTrue(EXAMPLES, "no documented commands to exercise")
        for ex in EXAMPLES:
            with self.subTest(op=ex["op"]):
                status, _, body = self.call(f"/api/{ex['op']}", ex["payload"])
                res = json.loads(body)
                self.assertEqual(status, 200, res)
                self.assertIn(res["exit_code"], (0, 1), res)
                self.assertTrue(res.get("stdout", "").strip() or res.get("files"), res)
                self.assertNotIn("Traceback", res.get("stdout", "") + res.get("error", ""))

    def test_unknown_commands_fields_and_bad_json_are_rejected(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.call("/api/not-a-command", {})[0], 404)
        op = SPEC["ops"][0]["id"]
        self.assertEqual(self.call(f"/api/{op}", {"definitely_not_a_field": 1})[0], 400)
        self.assertEqual(self.call(f"/api/{op}", raw=b"[1, 2")[0], 400)

    def test_oversized_body_is_refused(self):
        conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", self.srv.server_address[1], timeout=10)
        conn.putrequest("POST", f"/api/{SPEC['ops'][0]['id']}")
        conn.putheader("Content-Length", str(web.MAX_BODY + 1))
        conn.endheaders()
        self.assertEqual(conn.getresponse().status, 413)
        conn.close()

    def test_client_cannot_name_a_server_path(self):
        for op in SPEC["ops"]:
            for f in op["fields"]:
                if f["kind"] in ("file", "dir"):
                    status, _, body = self.call(f"/api/{op['id']}", {f["dest"]: "/etc/passwd"})
                    self.assertEqual(status, 400, body)
                    return
        self.skipTest("this product takes no file or folder inputs")

    def test_zip_path_traversal_is_blocked(self):
        buf = io.BytesIO()
        with zipfile.ZipFile(buf, "w") as z:
            z.writestr("../../escape.txt", "x")
        upload = {"base64": base64.b64encode(buf.getvalue()).decode()}
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t, self.assertRaises(web.BadRequest):
            web._write_upload({"dest": "d", "kind": "dir"}, upload, pathlib.Path(t))

    def test_user_text_never_becomes_an_option(self):
        op = {
            "prefix": ["x"],
            "fields": [
                {"dest": "v", "flag": None, "kind": "text", "required": True, "scope": "op"},
                {"dest": "o", "flag": "--o", "kind": "text", "scope": "op"},
            ],
        }
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as t:
            argv, _ = web.build_argv(op, {"v": "--evil", "o": "--also"}, pathlib.Path(t), pathlib.Path(t))
        self.assertEqual(argv[-2:], ["--", "--evil"])
        self.assertIn("--o=--also", argv)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

      "content": "# Architecture — vibe-lube\n\n## 1. Scope\nFast inspection and safe tune-ups for AI-built (\"vibe-coded\") apps.\n**MVP:** repository walker (skips vendored and build directories) with detectors for secrets, env\nhygiene, client-side secret exposure, supply chain, risky code and maintainability. Severity-weighted\nhealth score and grade, a service menu quote, and safe auto-fixes only (`.gitignore` env entries,\nnames-only `.env.example`).\n**Product:** GitHub App on every PR, runtime checks against the deployed URL, agent-generated fix PRs with human review.\n\n## 2. System context\n```mermaid\nflowchart LR\n  Repo[Repository] --> Walker\n  Walker --> Detectors[Detectors: secrets, env, client exposure, supply chain, risky code, maintainability]\n  Detectors --> Findings[(Findings)]\n  Findings --> Score[Score + grade]\n  Findings --> Menu[Service menu quote]\n  Findings --> Fixer[Safe auto-fixer]\n  Findings -->|book a mechanic| Human[Expert review]\n```\n\n## 3. Detector design\nEach detector is a pure function over a file's lines (plus repo-level checks), emitting\n`Finding{rule, severity, file, line, detail, fix}`. Secrets are **masked in findings**\n(`first6...last2`) so reports are safe to share. Severity points are critical 25, high 12,\nmedium 5, low 1.\n\n## 4. Design decisions\n- **Safe fixes only, automatically.** Anything that could break the app (rotating keys,\n  refactoring SQL) is a menu item for a human. Generated `.env.example` contains **names only, never values**.\n- **Client-side heuristics** (`src/`, `app/`, `pages/`, `components/` minus `/api/`) to flag\n  `service_role` and public-prefixed secrets. These are the most common catastrophic leaks in\n  Supabase and Next.js vibe apps.\n- **Placeholder suppression** (`example`, `xxxx`) cuts false positives in docs and tests.\n- **Exit code reflects grade** (A–C → 0, D–F → 1) so it can gate CI.\n\n## 5. Production architecture\nA GitHub App (webhooks → job queue → sandboxed scanner container → check-run annotations).\nRuntime probes (`/.env`, `/.git/config`, open Supabase tables via the anon key, missing RLS).\nA fix-PR generator (agent) behind mandatory human approval.\n\n## 6. Risks\nRegex secret detection has false positives and negatives, so entropy checks and provider-specific\nvalidators come next. Never transmit discovered secrets: masking happens at detection time.\n"

def _mask(s: str) -> str:
    return s[:6] + "..." + s[-2:] if len(s) > 10 else "***"


MAX_SCAN_BYTES = 2_000_000


def _walk(root):
    for r, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS and not (d.startswith(".") and d not in {".github"})]
        for f in files:
            yield os.path.join(r, f)


def _gitignored(root: str, rel: str) -> bool:
    """Does the root .gitignore ignore `rel`? Git semantics for the cases that matter for secrets.

    Last matching line wins, `!pattern` re-includes, a leading `/` anchors to the root, and a pattern
    without a slash matches the basename at any depth. Note `.env.*` does NOT ignore `.env` itself.
    """
    gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
    if not os.path.exists(gi):
        return False
    with open(gi, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
        patterns = [l.strip() for l in fh if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    rel = rel.replace("\\", "/")
    ignored = False
    for pat in patterns:
        negate = pat.startswith("!")
        pat = pat[1:] if negate else pat
        pat = pat.rstrip("/")
        if pat.startswith("/") or "/" in pat:
            hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(rel, pat.lstrip("/"))
        else:
            hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(os.path.basename(rel), pat)
        if hit:
            ignored = not negate
    return ignored


def inspect(root: str) -> Report:
    rep = Report(root=root, files_scanned=0)
    env_vars: set[str] = set()
    console_logs, todos = 0, 0
    has_tests = False

    def add(rule, sev, path, line, detail, fix):
        rep.findings.append(Finding(rule, sev, os.path.relpath(path, root).replace("\\", "/"), line, detail, fix))

    for path in _walk(root):
        rel = os.path.relpath(path, root).replace("\\", "/")

        ext = os.path.splitext(base)[1].lower()

            has_tests = True

        if is_env_file and not _gitignored(root, rel):
            add(
                "env_not_ignored",
                "critical",
                path,
                0,
                f"{base} is not in .gitignore",
                "Add it to .gitignore and rotate anything inside.",
            )
        if ext not in TEXT_EXTS and not base.startswith(".env"):
            continue
        try:
            if os.path.getsize(path) > MAX_SCAN_BYTES:  # minified bundles / data dumps: not worth the memory
                continue
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
                lines = fh.read().splitlines()
        except OSError:
            continue

        is_code = ext in CODE_EXTS
        is_client = (
            is_code

            and rel.startswith(CLIENT_HINTS)
            and "/api/" not in rel
        )
        if is_code and len(lines) > 1000:
            add("huge_file", "low", path, 0, f"{len(lines)} lines", "Split into smaller modules.")
        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):

                        add(

                            "critical",
                            path,
                            i,
                            f"{name}: {_mask(m.group(0))}",
                            "Rotate this key now, then load it from an environment variable.",

            pm = PUBLIC_SECRET.search(line)
            if pm:
                add(
                    "public_secret",
                    "critical",
                    path,
                    i,
                    f"{pm.group(0)} is bundled into the browser",
                    "Rename without the public prefix and use it only server-side.",

            if is_client and re.search(r"service_role|SERVICE_ROLE", line):

                    "service_role_client",
                    "critical",
                    path,
                    i,
                    "Supabase service_role used in client code",
                    "Use the anon key in the browser and protect tables with RLS.",

                    if rx.search(line):
                        add(rule, sev, path, i, line.strip()[:100], fix)
                if "console.log(" in line:
                    console_logs += 1
                if re.search(r"\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b", line):
                    todos += 1
        if base == "package.json":
            try:
                pkg = json.loads("\n".join(lines))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:

            d = os.path.dirname(path)
            if not any(
                os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, lf))
                for lf in ("package-lock.json", "yarn.lock", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "bun.lockb", "bun.lock")
            ):

                    "no_lockfile",
                    "medium",
                    path,
                    0,
                    "no lockfile next to package.json",
                    "Commit your lockfile so installs are reproducible.",
                )
            for section in ("dependencies", "devDependencies"):
                for dep, ver in (pkg.get(section) or {}).items():
                    if ver in {"*", "latest", ""}:
                        add("unpinned_dep", "medium", path, 0, f"{dep}@{ver}", "Pin to a specific version range.")

    if env_vars and not any(
        os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) for f in (".env.example", ".env.sample", ".env.template")
    ):
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding(
                "missing_env_example",
                "low",
                ".env.example",
                0,
                f"{len(env_vars)} env vars referenced, no .env.example",
                "Run with --fix to generate one.",
            )
        )
    if not has_tests:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding(
                "no_tests",
                "medium",
                "-",
                0,
                "no test files found",
                "Add smoke tests for sign-up, payment and core flows.",
            )
        )
    if not any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) for f in ("README.md", "readme.md", "README")):
        rep.findings.append(Finding("no_readme", "low", "-", 0, "no README", "Document how to run and deploy the app."))
    if console_logs > 10:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding("console_logs", "low", "-", 0, f"{console_logs} console.log calls", "Remove or gate debug logging.")
        )
    if todos > 10:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding("todos", "low", "-", 0, f"{todos} TODO/FIXME markers", "Turn them into tracked issues.")
        )

    rep.env_vars = sorted(env_vars)
    sev_rank = {"critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 3}
    rep.findings.sort(key=lambda f: (sev_rank[f.severity], f.file, f.line))
    penalty = sum(SEVERITY_POINTS[f.severity] for f in rep.findings)
    rep.score = max(0, 100 - penalty)
    rep.grade = (
        "A"
        if rep.score >= 90
        else "B"
        if rep.score >= 75
        else "C"
        if rep.score >= 60
        else "D"
        if rep.score >= 40
        else "F"
    )
    rules = {f.rule for f in rep.findings}
    rep.quote_minutes = sum(SERVICE_MENU[r][1] for r in rules)
    rep.quote_usd = sum(SERVICE_MENU[r][2] for r in rules)
    return rep


def apply_safe_fixes(root: str, rep: Report) -> list[str]:
    """Only non-destructive fixes: git-ignore env files, write .env.example with names (never values)."""
    done = []
    rules = {f.rule for f in rep.findings}
    if "env_not_ignored" in rules:
        gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
        existing = ""
        if os.path.exists(gi):
            with open(gi, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
                existing = fh.read()
        add = [p for p in (".env", ".env.*", "!.env.example") if p not in existing.split()]
        with open(gi, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(("\n" if existing and not existing.endswith("\n") else "") + "\n".join(add) + "\n")
        done.append(f"added {', '.join(add)} to .gitignore (rotate any keys that were committed!)")
    if "missing_env_example" in rules and rep.env_vars:
        try:  # "x": never overwrite a .env.example the user already has
            with open(os.path.join(root, ".env.example"), "x", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write("# Generated by vibe-lube - fill in real values in .env (never commit it)\n")
                fh.write("".join(f"{v}=\n" for v in rep.env_vars))
            done.append(f"wrote .env.example with {len(rep.env_vars)} variables")
        except FileExistsError:
            done.append("left existing .env.example untouched")
    return done
"
     },
     {
      "name": "vibe_lube/web.py",
      "content": """"Hosted API and web app for this product, generated from its CLI (shared runtime, identical in every product).

Every CLI command becomes POST /api/<command> (JSON in, JSON out) and a form at GET /. Each request runs the
real CLI in an isolated subprocess with a timeout, so the web app and the CLI can never disagree.

Security model:
- File and folder arguments come only from uploads written into a private per-request directory; a client can
  never name a path on the server. Folder uploads are zip archives extracted with path-traversal checks.
- Values are passed as separate argv items, options as --flag=value and positionals after "--", so user text
  can never become an option or a shell command.
- State/store options are pinned by the server to its data directory (--data-dir), never client-controlled.
- 5 MB request cap, 30 s run timeout, CSP / nosniff / frame-deny headers, binds 127.0.0.1 unless --host is set.

Run:  <product>-web --port 8000 [--host 0.0.0.0] [--data-dir ./data]
"""

PKG = __package__ or "app"

OPS = {op["id"]: op for op in SPEC["ops"]}
MAX_BODY = 5 * 1024 * 1024
TIMEOUT = 30
HEADERS = {
    "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
    "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
    "Referrer-Policy": "no-referrer",
    "Content-Security-Policy": "default-src 'none'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; "
    "connect-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'",
}


class BadRequest(ValueError):
    pass


def _write_upload(field: dict, value, workdir: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    """Materialise an uploaded file or folder inside workdir and return its path."""
    if not isinstance(value, dict):
        raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: expected an upload object")
    if field["kind"] == "dir":
        target = workdir / f"in-{field['dest']}"
        target.mkdir()
        if "files" in value:  # [{"name": "a.txt", "content": "..."}]
            for f in value["files"]:
                _safe_member(target, str(f.get("name", ""))).write_text(str(f.get("content", "")), encoding="utf-8")
        elif "base64" in value:  # a zip archive
            try:
                with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(base64.b64decode(value["base64"], validate=True))) as z:
                    for info in z.infolist():
                        if not info.is_dir():
                            _safe_member(target, info.filename).write_bytes(z.read(info))
            except (zipfile.BadZipFile, ValueError) as e:
                raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: not a valid zip archive ({e})") from None
        else:
            raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: folder uploads need 'files' or a base64 zip")
        return str(target)
    name = pathlib.PurePath(str(value.get("name") or field["dest"])).name or field["dest"]
    path = workdir / f"in-{field['dest']}-{name}"
    if "base64" in value:
        try:
            path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(value["base64"], validate=True))
        except ValueError:
            raise BadRequest(f"{field['dest']}: invalid base64") from None
    else:
        path.write_text(str(value.get("content", "")), encoding="utf-8")
    return str(path)


def _safe_member(root: pathlib.Path, name: str) -> pathlib.Path:
    dest = (root / name).resolve()
    if root.resolve() not in dest.parents:
        raise BadRequest(f"unsafe path in upload: {name!r}")
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return dest


def build_argv(op: dict, payload: dict, workdir: pathlib.Path, data_dir: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[list, dict]:
    """Translate a JSON payload into CLI argv. Returns (argv, outputs) where outputs maps dest -> output path."""
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise BadRequest("request body must be a JSON object")
    unknown = set(payload) - {f["dest"] for f in op["fields"]}
    if unknown:
        raise BadRequest(f"unknown fields: {sorted(unknown)}")
    head, opts, pos, outputs = [], [], [], {}
    for flag, filename in SPEC.get("state", {}).items():  # server-pinned stores go before the subcommand
        head.append(f"{flag}={data_dir / filename}")
    for f in op["fields"]:
        kind, value = f["kind"], payload.get(f["dest"])
        if kind == "output":
            value = str(workdir / f"out-{f['dest']}")
            outputs[f["dest"]] = value
        elif kind == "state":  # a per-command store: always the server's own file, never client-chosen
            value = str(data_dir / f["file"])
        elif value is None or value == "" or value == []:
            if f.get("required"):
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} is required")
            continue
        elif kind in ("file", "dir"):
            value = _write_upload(f, value, workdir)
        elif kind == "bool":
            if value is True:
                (head if f.get("scope") == "global" else opts).append(f["flag"])
            continue
        elif kind in ("int", "number"):
            try:
                value = str(int(value) if kind == "int" else float(value))
            except (TypeError, ValueError):
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} must be a number") from None
        elif kind == "list":
            values = value if isinstance(value, list) else [value]
            if f.get("choices") and any(str(v) not in f["choices"] for v in values):
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} must be among {f['choices']}")
            if f["flag"] is None:
                pos.extend(str(v) for v in values)
            elif f.get("append"):
                opts.extend(f"{f['flag']}={v}" for v in values)
            elif values:  # nargs list option: items follow the flag, so none may look like an option
                if any(str(v).startswith("-") for v in values):
                    raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} items cannot start with '-'")
                opts.extend([f["flag"], *[str(v) for v in values]])
            continue
        else:
            value = str(value)
            if f.get("choices") and value not in f["choices"]:
                raise BadRequest(f"{f['dest']} must be one of {f['choices']}")
        if f["flag"] is None:
            pos.append(value)
        else:
            (head if f.get("scope") == "global" else opts).append(f"{f['flag']}={value}")
    # positionals after "--" so user text that starts with "-" can never be read as an option
    argv = [*head, *op["prefix"], *opts]
    if pos:
        argv += ["--", *pos]
    return argv, outputs


def run_op(op: dict, payload: dict, data_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="web-") as tmp:
        work = pathlib.Path(tmp)
        argv, outputs = build_argv(op, payload, work, data_dir)
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "AGENT_ECONOMY_DEBUG"}
        env.update(PYTHONIOENCODING="utf-8", HOME=str(data_dir), USERPROFILE=str(data_dir))
        try:
            r = subprocess.run(
                [sys.executable, "-m", PKG, *argv],
                cwd=work,
                env=env,
                capture_output=True,
                text=True,
                encoding="utf-8",
                errors="replace",
                timeout=TIMEOUT,
            )
        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
            return {"ok": False, "exit_code": None, "error": f"timed out after {TIMEOUT}s"}
        # exit 1 is a domain answer ("nothing found", "failing grade") only when the command said something;
        # a silent exit 1 is a failure, and stderr is always passed through so the user sees why
        # never echo the server's private temp paths back to the client
        r.stdout = r.stdout.replace(str(work), "upload").replace(str(work.resolve()), "upload")
        r.stderr = r.stderr.replace(str(work), "upload").replace(str(work.resolve()), "upload")
        said = bool(r.stdout.strip())
        result = {
            "ok": r.returncode == 0 or (r.returncode == 1 and said),
            "exit_code": r.returncode,
            "stdout": r.stdout[-200_000:],
        }
        if r.stderr.strip():
            result["stderr"] = r.stderr.strip()[-2000:]
        if not result["ok"]:
            result["error"] = result.get("stderr") or "command failed without output"
        with contextlib.suppress(ValueError):
            result["json"] = json.loads(r.stdout)
        for dest, path in outputs.items():
            p = pathlib.Path(path)
            if p.is_file():
                result.setdefault("files", {})[dest] = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[-500_000:]
        return result


class Gate:
    """API keys, a per-caller rate limit and usage metering (the record billing is built on).

    Keys come from API_KEYS (comma-separated) and/or <data-dir>/api-keys.json, which stores only SHA-256
    hashes. With no keys configured the API is open, which `main` allows only on a loopback address.
    """

    def __init__(self, data_dir: pathlib.Path, env_keys: str = "", rate_per_min: int = 60):
        self.keys_file, self.usage_file = data_dir / "api-keys.json", data_dir / "usage.jsonl"
        self.env = {_digest(k.strip()): f"env-{i}" for i, k in enumerate(env_keys.split(","), 1) if k.strip()}
        self.rate = rate_per_min
        self.hits: dict[str, list[float]] = {}
        self.lock = threading.Lock()

    def stored(self) -> dict:
        try:
            data = json.loads(self.keys_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            return {}
        return data if isinstance(data, dict) else {}

    def active(self) -> dict:
        """hash -> key id for every key that may call the API."""
        keys = dict(self.env)
        keys.update({rec["hash"]: kid for kid, rec in self.stored().items() if not rec.get("revoked")})
        return keys

    def required(self) -> bool:
        return bool(self.active())

    def identify(self, header: str | None) -> str | None:
        if not header or not header.startswith("Bearer "):
            return None
        digest = _digest(header[7:].strip())
        found = None
        for h, kid in self.active().items():  # compare every key in constant time; never short-circuit
            if hmac.compare_digest(h, digest):
                found = kid
        return found

    def retry_after(self, caller: str) -> int | None:
        """Sliding one-minute window; returns seconds to wait when the caller is over the limit."""
        now = time.monotonic()
        with self.lock:
            window = [t for t in self.hits.get(caller, []) if now - t < 60]
            if len(window) >= self.rate:
                self.hits[caller] = window
                return max(1, int(60 - (now - window[0])) + 1)
            window.append(now)
            self.hits[caller] = window
        return None

    def record(self, caller: str, op: str, status: int, ms: int):
        line = json.dumps(
            {
                "ts": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
                "key": caller,
                "op": op,
                "status": status,
                "ms": ms,
            }
        )
        with self.lock, open(self.usage_file, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(line + "\n")

    def create(self, label: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
        key = "sk_" + secrets.token_urlsafe(24)
        digest = _digest(key)
        kid = digest[:10]
        keys = self.stored()
        keys[kid] = {"hash": digest, "label": label, "created": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d"), "revoked": False}
        self._save(keys)
        return kid, key

    def revoke(self, kid: str) -> bool:
        keys = self.stored()
        if kid not in keys:
            return False
        keys[kid]["revoked"] = True
        self._save(keys)
        return True

    def _save(self, keys: dict):
        tmp = self.keys_file.with_suffix(".tmp")
        tmp.write_text(json.dumps(keys, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
        os.replace(tmp, self.keys_file)

    def usage(self) -> dict:
        summary: dict[str, dict] = {}
        try:
            lines = self.usage_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        except OSError:
            return summary
        for ln in lines:
            with contextlib.suppress(ValueError, KeyError):
                rec = json.loads(ln)
                s = summary.setdefault(rec["key"], {"calls": 0, "ok": 0, "by_op": {}})
                s["calls"] += 1
                s["ok"] += rec["status"] == 200
                s["by_op"][rec["op"]] = s["by_op"].get(rec["op"], 0) + 1
        return summary


def _digest(key: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(key.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server_version = f"{PKG}-web"
    data_dir: pathlib.Path
    gate: Gate

    def _send(self, status: int, body: bytes, ctype: str, extra: dict | None = None):
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", ctype)
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        for k, v in {**HEADERS, **(extra or {})}.items():
            self.send_header(k, v)
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _json(self, status: int, obj, extra: dict | None = None):
        body = json.dumps(obj, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
        self._send(status, body, "application/json; charset=utf-8", extra)

    def log_message(self, fmt, *args):  # one line per request on stderr, no bodies
        sys.stderr.write(f"{self.address_string()} {fmt % args}\n")

    def do_GET(self):
        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
        if path == "/healthz":
            self._json(200, {"status": "ok", "product": SPEC["name"]})
        elif path == "/api/spec":
            self._json(200, SPEC)
        elif path == "/app.js":
            self._send(200, APP_JS.encode("utf-8"), "text/javascript; charset=utf-8")
        elif path in ("/", "/index.html"):
            self._send(200, page().encode("utf-8"), "text/html; charset=utf-8")
        else:
            self._json(404, {"error": "not found"})

    def do_POST(self):
        path = self.path.split("?", 1)[0]
        try:
            length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
        except ValueError:
            return self._json(400, {"error": "bad Content-Length"})
        if length > MAX_BODY:
            return self._json(HTTPStatus.REQUEST_ENTITY_TOO_LARGE, {"error": f"request over {MAX_BODY} bytes"})
        # always read the body before answering: closing with unread data makes some stacks reset the connection
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        op = OPS.get(path.removeprefix("/api/")) if path.startswith("/api/") else None
        if not op:
            return self._json(404, {"error": "unknown command", "commands": sorted(OPS)})
        caller = self.gate.identify(self.headers.get("Authorization"))
        if caller is None and self.gate.required():
            self.gate.record("unauthenticated", op["id"], 401, 0)
            return self._json(401, {"error": "missing or invalid API key"}, {"WWW-Authenticate": "Bearer"})
        caller = caller or f"ip:{self.client_address[0]}"
        wait = self.gate.retry_after(caller)
        if wait:
            return self._json(
                429, {"error": f"rate limit: {self.gate.rate} requests per minute"}, {"Retry-After": str(wait)}
            )
        started = time.monotonic()
        try:
            payload = json.loads(body or b"{}")
            result = run_op(op, payload, self.data_dir)
            status = 200
        except (ValueError, BadRequest) as e:
            result, status = {"error": str(e)}, 400
        self.gate.record(caller, op["id"], status, int((time.monotonic() - started) * 1000))
        self._json(status, result)

def make_server(
    host: str, port: int, data_dir: pathlib.Path, env_keys: str = "", rate: int = 60
) -> ThreadingHTTPServer:
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gate = Gate(data_dir.resolve(), env_keys, rate)
    handler = type("BoundHandler", (Handler,), {"data_dir": data_dir.resolve(), "gate": gate})
    return ThreadingHTTPServer((host, port), handler)


def keys_main(argv: list) -> int:
    """<cli>-web keys create|list|revoke and <cli>-web usage: manage API keys and read metering."""
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=f"{SPEC['cli']}-web")
    ap.add_argument("--data-dir", default=os.environ.get("DATA_DIR", "data"))
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    k = sub.add_parser("keys").add_subparsers(dest="action", required=True)
    k.add_parser("create").add_argument("--label", required=True, help="who the key is for, e.g. a customer")
    k.add_parser("list")
    k.add_parser("revoke").add_argument("key_id")
    sub.add_parser("usage", help="calls per key, for billing")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    data_dir = pathlib.Path(a.data_dir)
    data_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    gate = Gate(data_dir.resolve())
    if a.cmd == "usage":
        print(json.dumps(gate.usage(), indent=2))
    elif a.action == "create":
        kid, key = gate.create(a.label)
        print(f"key id {kid} for {a.label!r}\n{key}\nShown once; only its hash is stored.")
    elif a.action == "list":
        for kid, rec in gate.stored().items():
            print(f"{kid}  {rec['created']}  {'REVOKED ' if rec.get('revoked') else ''}{rec['label']}")
    elif not gate.revoke(a.key_id):
        print(f"no key {a.key_id!r}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    else:
        print(f"revoked {a.key_id}")
    return 0


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    argv = sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv
    if argv[:1] in (["keys"], ["usage"]) or (len(argv) > 2 and argv[2] in ("keys", "usage")):
        return keys_main(argv)
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=f"{SPEC['cli']}-web", description=f"{SPEC['name']} hosted API and web app")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--host", default="127.0.0.1", help="use 0.0.0.0 to accept outside connections (e.g. in a container)"
    )
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("PORT", "8000")))
    ap.add_argument("--data-dir", default=os.environ.get("DATA_DIR", "data"), help="where server-side state is kept")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--rate", type=int, default=int(os.environ.get("RATE_LIMIT_PER_MIN", "60")), help="calls/min per caller"
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--allow-public",
        action="store_true",
        default=os.environ.get("ALLOW_PUBLIC") == "1",
        help="serve a non-loopback address without API keys (not recommended)",
    )
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    srv = make_server(a.host, a.port, pathlib.Path(a.data_dir), os.environ.get("API_KEYS", ""), a.rate)
    gate = srv.RequestHandlerClass.gate
    if a.host not in LOOPBACK and not gate.required() and not a.allow_public:
        srv.server_close()
        print(
            f"refusing to serve {a.host} with no API keys: run `{SPEC['cli']}-web keys create --label NAME` "
            "or set API_KEYS (or pass --allow-public)",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        return 2
    access = "API keys required" if gate.required() else "open (no API keys)"
    print(
        f"{SPEC['name']} on http://{a.host}:{srv.server_address[1]}  ({access}; data: {pathlib.Path(a.data_dir).resolve()})"
    )
    with contextlib.suppress(KeyboardInterrupt):
        srv.serve_forever()
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

## What it does

  - **env hygiene**: `.env` present but not git-ignored; env vars referenced in code

  - **client-side exposure**: `NEXT_PUBLIC_` / `VITE_` vars named like secrets,
    Supabase `service_role` in client code
  - **supply chain**: `package.json` without a lockfile, `"*"` / `"latest"` versions
  - **risky code**: `eval(`, SQL built with string concatenation / f-strings,

"""Static inspection of AI-built ("vibe-coded") apps, with safe auto-fixes."""

from __future__ import annotations

import fnmatch
import json
import os
import re
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field

__all__ = ["Finding", "Report", "inspect", "apply_safe_fixes", "SERVICE_MENU"]

SKIP_DIRS = {
    ".git",
    "node_modules",
    "dist",
    "build",
    ".next",
    ".venv",
    "venv",
    "__pycache__",
    ".turbo",
    "coverage",
    ".vercel",
}
CODE_EXTS = {
    ".js",
    ".jsx",
    ".ts",
    ".tsx",
    ".mjs",
    ".cjs",
    ".py",
    ".rb",
    ".go",
    ".php",
    ".vue",
    ".svelte",
    ".java",
    ".cs",
}
TEXT_EXTS = CODE_EXTS | {".json", ".yml", ".yaml", ".toml", ".env", ".md", ".html", ".sh", ".txt", ".ini", ".cfg"}
CLIENT_HINTS = ("src/", "app/", "pages/", "components/", "public/", "client/", "frontend/")

SECRET_PATTERNS = [
    ("anthropic_key", re.compile(r"sk-ant-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,}")),
    ("openai_key", re.compile(r"sk-(?:proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9_-]{32,}")),
    ("aws_access_key", re.compile(r"\bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b")),
    ("github_token", re.compile(r"\bgh[pousr]_[A-Za-z0-9]{36,}\b")),
    ("slack_token", re.compile(r"\bxox[abprs]-[A-Za-z0-9-]{10,}")),
    ("stripe_secret", re.compile(r"\bsk_live_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,}")),
    ("private_key", re.compile(r"-----BEGIN (?:RSA |EC |OPENSSH |)PRIVATE KEY-----")),
    ("generic_secret", re.compile(r"""(?i)\b(?:api[_-]?key|secret|password|token)\b\s*[:=]\s*["'][^"'\s]{12,}["']""")),
]
ENV_REF = re.compile(
    r"process\.env\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)|import\.meta\.env\.([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)|os\.environ(?:\.get)?\(\s*[\"']([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)|os\.getenv\(\s*[\"']([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)|os\.environ\[\s*[\"']([A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+)"
)
PUBLIC_SECRET = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:NEXT_PUBLIC|VITE|REACT_APP|EXPO_PUBLIC)_[A-Z0-9_]*(?:SECRET|PRIVATE|SERVICE_ROLE|PASSWORD)[A-Z0-9_]*"
)
RISKY = [
    ("eval", "high", re.compile(r"(?<![\w.])eval\s*\("), "Remove eval(); parse data with JSON.parse or a real parser."),
    (
        "sql_concat",
        "high",
        re.compile(
            r"""(?i)(?:execute|query|raw)\s*\(\s*(?:f["']|["'][^"']*(?:select|insert|update|delete)[^"']*["']\s*\+)"""
        ),
        "Use parameterised queries instead of building SQL strings.",
    ),
    (
        "cors_wildcard",
        "medium",
        re.compile(
            r"""(?i)(?:access-control-allow-origin["']?\s*[:,]\s*["']\*|cors\(\s*\)|origin\s*:\s*["']\*["']|allow_origins\s*=\s*\[\s*["']\*)"""
        ),
        "Restrict CORS to your real domains.",
    ),
    (
        "debug_mode",
        "medium",
        re.compile(r"(?i)\bdebug\s*=\s*true\b|app\.run\([^)]*debug\s*=\s*True"),
        "Turn off debug mode in production.",
    ),
]
SEVERITY_POINTS = {"critical": 25, "high": 12, "medium": 5, "low": 1}

SERVICE_MENU = {
    "secret_in_code": ("Rotate key + move to env var", 30, 49),
    "env_not_ignored": ("Git-ignore .env, scrub history", 20, 39),
    "missing_env_example": ("Generate .env.example", 5, 0),
    "public_secret": ("Move secret to server-side route", 45, 79),
    "service_role_client": ("Replace service_role with anon key + RLS", 60, 99),
    "no_lockfile": ("Add lockfile, pin deps", 10, 19),
    "unpinned_dep": ("Pin dependency versions", 10, 19),
    "eval": ("Remove eval", 20, 39),
    "sql_concat": ("Parameterise SQL queries", 30, 59),
    "cors_wildcard": ("Lock down CORS", 10, 19),
    "debug_mode": ("Disable debug in prod", 5, 9),
    "no_tests": ("Add smoke tests for critical flows", 90, 149),
    "no_readme": ("Write README + run instructions", 15, 19),
    "huge_file": ("Split oversized file", 45, 69),
    "console_logs": ("Strip debug logging", 10, 9),
    "todos": ("Triage TODOs into issues", 15, 0),
}


@dataclass
class Finding:
    rule: str
    severity: str
    file: str
    line: int
    detail: str
    fix: str


@dataclass
class Report:
    root: str
    files_scanned: int
    findings: list = field(default_factory=list)
    score: int = 100
    grade: str = "A"
    env_vars: list = field(default_factory=list)
    quote_minutes: int = 0
    quote_usd: int = 0

    def to_dict(self):
        return asdict(self)


def _mask(s: str) -> str:
    return s[:6] + "..." + s[-2:] if len(s) > 10 else "***"


MAX_SCAN_BYTES = 2_000_000


def _walk(root):
    for r, dirs, files in os.walk(root):
        dirs[:] = [d for d in dirs if d not in SKIP_DIRS and not (d.startswith(".") and d not in {".github"})]
        for f in files:
            yield os.path.join(r, f)


def _gitignored(root: str, rel: str) -> bool:
    """Does the root .gitignore ignore `rel`? Git semantics for the cases that matter for secrets.

    Last matching line wins, `!pattern` re-includes, a leading `/` anchors to the root, and a pattern
    without a slash matches the basename at any depth. Note `.env.*` does NOT ignore `.env` itself.
    """
    gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
    if not os.path.exists(gi):
        return False
    with open(gi, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
        patterns = [l.strip() for l in fh if l.strip() and not l.lstrip().startswith("#")]
    rel = rel.replace("\\", "/")
    ignored = False
    for pat in patterns:
        negate = pat.startswith("!")
        pat = pat[1:] if negate else pat
        pat = pat.rstrip("/")
        if pat.startswith("/") or "/" in pat:
            hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(rel, pat.lstrip("/"))
        else:
            hit = fnmatch.fnmatchcase(os.path.basename(rel), pat)
        if hit:
            ignored = not negate
    return ignored


def inspect(root: str) -> Report:
    rep = Report(root=root, files_scanned=0)
    env_vars: set[str] = set()
    console_logs, todos = 0, 0
    has_tests = False

    def add(rule, sev, path, line, detail, fix):
        rep.findings.append(Finding(rule, sev, os.path.relpath(path, root).replace("\\", "/"), line, detail, fix))

    for path in _walk(root):
        rel = os.path.relpath(path, root).replace("\\", "/")
        base = os.path.basename(path)
        ext = os.path.splitext(base)[1].lower()
        if re.search(r"(^|/)(tests?|__tests__|spec)(/|$)|\.(test|spec)\.\w+$|^test_.*\.py$", rel):
            has_tests = True
        is_env_file = base.startswith(".env") and base not in {".env.example", ".env.sample", ".env.template"}
        if is_env_file and not _gitignored(root, rel):
            add(
                "env_not_ignored",
                "critical",
                path,
                0,
                f"{base} is not in .gitignore",
                "Add it to .gitignore and rotate anything inside.",
            )
        if ext not in TEXT_EXTS and not base.startswith(".env"):
            continue
        try:
            if os.path.getsize(path) > MAX_SCAN_BYTES:  # minified bundles / data dumps: not worth the memory
                continue
            with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="ignore") as fh:
                lines = fh.read().splitlines()
        except OSError:
            continue
        rep.files_scanned += 1
        is_code = ext in CODE_EXTS
        is_client = (
            is_code
            and ext in {".js", ".jsx", ".ts", ".tsx", ".vue", ".svelte", ".mjs"}
            and rel.startswith(CLIENT_HINTS)
            and "/api/" not in rel
        )
        if is_code and len(lines) > 1000:
            add("huge_file", "low", path, 0, f"{len(lines)} lines", "Split into smaller modules.")
        for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
            if not base.startswith(".env") and base not in {".env.example"}:
                for name, rx in SECRET_PATTERNS:
                    m = rx.search(line)
                    if m and "example" not in line.lower() and "xxxx" not in m.group(0).lower():
                        add(
                            "secret_in_code",
                            "critical",
                            path,
                            i,
                            f"{name}: {_mask(m.group(0))}",
                            "Rotate this key now, then load it from an environment variable.",
                        )
                        break
            for m in ENV_REF.finditer(line):
                env_vars.add(next(g for g in m.groups() if g))
            pm = PUBLIC_SECRET.search(line)
            if pm:
                add(
                    "public_secret",
                    "critical",
                    path,
                    i,
                    f"{pm.group(0)} is bundled into the browser",
                    "Rename without the public prefix and use it only server-side.",
                )
            if is_client and re.search(r"service_role|SERVICE_ROLE", line):
                add(
                    "service_role_client",
                    "critical",
                    path,
                    i,
                    "Supabase service_role used in client code",
                    "Use the anon key in the browser and protect tables with RLS.",
                )
            if is_code:
                for rule, sev, rx, fix in RISKY:
                    if rx.search(line):
                        add(rule, sev, path, i, line.strip()[:100], fix)
                if "console.log(" in line:
                    console_logs += 1
                if re.search(r"\b(TODO|FIXME|HACK)\b", line):
                    todos += 1
        if base == "package.json":
            try:
                pkg = json.loads("\n".join(lines))
            except json.JSONDecodeError:
                pkg = {}
            d = os.path.dirname(path)
            if not any(
                os.path.exists(os.path.join(d, lf))
                for lf in ("package-lock.json", "yarn.lock", "pnpm-lock.yaml", "bun.lockb", "bun.lock")
            ):
                add(
                    "no_lockfile",
                    "medium",
                    path,
                    0,
                    "no lockfile next to package.json",
                    "Commit your lockfile so installs are reproducible.",
                )
            for section in ("dependencies", "devDependencies"):
                for dep, ver in (pkg.get(section) or {}).items():
                    if ver in {"*", "latest", ""}:
                        add("unpinned_dep", "medium", path, 0, f"{dep}@{ver}", "Pin to a specific version range.")

    if env_vars and not any(
        os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) for f in (".env.example", ".env.sample", ".env.template")
    ):
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding(
                "missing_env_example",
                "low",
                ".env.example",
                0,
                f"{len(env_vars)} env vars referenced, no .env.example",
                "Run with --fix to generate one.",
            )
        )
    if not has_tests:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding(
                "no_tests",
                "medium",
                "-",
                0,
                "no test files found",
                "Add smoke tests for sign-up, payment and core flows.",
            )
        )
    if not any(os.path.exists(os.path.join(root, f)) for f in ("README.md", "readme.md", "README")):
        rep.findings.append(Finding("no_readme", "low", "-", 0, "no README", "Document how to run and deploy the app."))
    if console_logs > 10:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding("console_logs", "low", "-", 0, f"{console_logs} console.log calls", "Remove or gate debug logging.")
        )
    if todos > 10:
        rep.findings.append(
            Finding("todos", "low", "-", 0, f"{todos} TODO/FIXME markers", "Turn them into tracked issues.")
        )

    rep.env_vars = sorted(env_vars)
    sev_rank = {"critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 3}
    rep.findings.sort(key=lambda f: (sev_rank[f.severity], f.file, f.line))
    penalty = sum(SEVERITY_POINTS[f.severity] for f in rep.findings)
    rep.score = max(0, 100 - penalty)
    rep.grade = (
        "A"
        if rep.score >= 90
        else "B"
        if rep.score >= 75
        else "C"
        if rep.score >= 60
        else "D"
        if rep.score >= 40
        else "F"
    )
    rules = {f.rule for f in rep.findings}
    rep.quote_minutes = sum(SERVICE_MENU[r][1] for r in rules)
    rep.quote_usd = sum(SERVICE_MENU[r][2] for r in rules)
    return rep


def apply_safe_fixes(root: str, rep: Report) -> list[str]:
    """Only non-destructive fixes: git-ignore env files, write .env.example with names (never values)."""
    done = []
    rules = {f.rule for f in rep.findings}
    if "env_not_ignored" in rules:
        gi = os.path.join(root, ".gitignore")
        existing = ""
        if os.path.exists(gi):
            with open(gi, encoding="utf-8-sig") as fh:
                existing = fh.read()
        add = [p for p in (".env", ".env.*", "!.env.example") if p not in existing.split()]
        with open(gi, "a", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            fh.write(("\n" if existing and not existing.endswith("\n") else "") + "\n".join(add) + "\n")
        done.append(f"added {', '.join(add)} to .gitignore (rotate any keys that were committed!)")
    if "missing_env_example" in rules and rep.env_vars:
        try:  # "x": never overwrite a .env.example the user already has
            with open(os.path.join(root, ".env.example"), "x", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                fh.write("# Generated by vibe-lube - fill in real values in .env (never commit it)\n")
                fh.write("".join(f"{v}=\n" for v in rep.env_vars))
            done.append(f"wrote .env.example with {len(rep.env_vars)} variables")
        except FileExistsError:
            done.append("left existing .env.example untouched")
    return done
